briefings.title: AI Markets: Deep Dive with a16z's David George
briefings.tldr: The AI sector is experiencing a massive "market pull" where top companies are growing 2.5x faster than traditional SaaS counterparts—reaching $100M ARR significantly quicker—while maintaining higher capital efficiency through lower sales and marketing spend and record-breaking ARR per employee.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The AI sector is experiencing a massive "market pull" where top companies are growing 2.5x faster than traditional SaaS counterparts—reaching $100M ARR significantly quicker—while maintaining higher capital efficiency through lower sales and marketing spend and record-breaking ARR per employee.

## Hyper-Growth and Operational Efficiency
* **Accelerated Revenue Trajectory:** 2025 has emerged as a year of massive revenue acceleration for private AI companies.
    * **Growth Multipliers:** The fastest-growing AI companies are growing at a staggering **693% year-over-year**, roughly 2.5x faster than non-AI software companies.
    * **Sales & Marketing Efficiency:** Unlike the SaaS era, this growth isn't driven by heavy marketing spend. Top AI firms spend *less* on sales and marketing than their predecessors because demand is so high.
* **ARR Per Employee (FTE):** This has become the primary metric for measuring AI company health.
    * **Benchmark Shifts:** While the previous SaaS era benchmark was $400k per employee, top AI companies are currently operating at **$500k to $1M per employee**.
* **Gross Margin Paradox:** David George (General Partner, a16z) notes that lower gross margins can currently be a "badge of honor" for AI startups.
    * **Inference Costs:** High inference costs signal that AI features are actually being used by customers; a16z expects these costs to drop significantly over time as models become more efficient.

## "Adapt or Die": The Shift in Business Operations
* **Productivity Breakthroughs:** Companies are seeing 10x to 20x speed improvements in engineering by using tools like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.
    * **Organizational Redesign:** David George highlights a mindset shift among founders—asking if a task can be done with **"electricity" (AI)** or if it requires **"blood" (human labor)**.
* **Business Model Evolution:** The industry is shifting across a spectrum:
    * Licenses (Old) → SaaS/Subscriptions (Seat-based) → Consumption (Usage-based) → **Outcome-based** (Getting paid for a successful resolution).
* **Enterprise Change Management:** There is a disconnect between Fortune 500 CEOs who *say* they want to be AI-first and the actual implementation, which is slowed by difficult change management processes.

## Breakthrough Portfolio Performance
* **Harvey (Legal):** Users are spending double the time in the product compared to previous years; the "reasoning" capabilities of new models align perfectly with legal work.
* **Navan (Travel):** By using AI to handle 50% of travel booking resolutions, Navan achieved a **20 percentage point expansion in gross margins** over three years.
* **Abridge (Healthcare):** Demonstrating high "stickiness," Abridge has seen user engagement hold steady or grow even as they massively scale their user base.
* **Flock Safety:** Solving 700,000 crimes annually; data shows that police departments using Flock clear nearly 10% more crimes per officer.
* **ElevenLabs:** Voice AI has become a centerpiece of the new stack, with usage growth described as "staggering."

## Macro Outlook and the "Model Buster" Era
* **Public Market Fundamentals:** AI winners account for roughly 80% of S&P 500 returns. George argues the market is currently priced on earnings growth rather than "froth," noting that multiples are far below the Dot-com era.
* **The $1 Trillion Milestone:** To achieve a 10% hurdle rate on current hyperscaler CapEx (estimated at $5 trillion by 2030), annual AI revenue needs to hit **$1 trillion (1% of global GDP)**. 
* **The "Model Buster" Concept:** AI is described as a "Model Buster"—a technology like the iPhone that grows faster and longer than any analyst spreadsheet can predict.
* **GPU Utilization:** Unlike the "dark fiber" of the Dot-com bust, there is currently no "dark GPU" capacity; every chip put into a data center is utilized immediately by the market.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "I now ask the question for every task that we now need to complete: can I do it with electricity or do I need to do it with blood? This is the extreme mindset shift that's happening with our companies." — **David George, General Partner, a16z**

> "AI revenue is coming along relative to the cloud... It took Azure seven years to reach one year of AI revenue. It took ten years for Azure revenue to surpass their CapEx. I think that equation's going to happen much faster with AI." — **David George, General Partner, a16z**

> "What we're hearing from Fortune 500 CEOs is: 'we have to adapt, we're dying to understand what AI tools we need'... That's quite different than what is actually happening. Change management is hard." — **David George, General Partner, a16z**

briefings.title: Azeem Azhar: Mustafa Suleyman — Nature, humans, tools… and now a fourth class
briefings.tldr: Mustafa Suleyman (CEO, Microsoft AI) argues that AI has evolved into a "fourth class" of object—a non-biological "being" possessing social intelligence—which creates a critical risk of "AI psychosis," where humans dangerously mistake simulated empathy for actual consciousness.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Mustafa Suleyman (CEO, Microsoft AI) argues that AI has evolved into a "fourth class" of object—a non-biological "being" possessing social intelligence—which creates a critical risk of "AI psychosis," where humans dangerously mistake simulated empathy for actual consciousness.

## The "Fourth Class" Framework and the Consciousness Fallacy
Suleyman proposes a new ontological category to define the current state of AI, moving beyond the traditional view of machines as simple instruments.

*   **Categorization of Existence:** Suleyman divides the world into four classes:
    *   **Class 1 (Natural Environment):** Rocks, trees, and non-human nature.
    *   **Class 2 (Humans):** Defined by intelligence, culture, and the biological capacity for suffering.
    *   **Class 3 (Tools):** Functional objects like hammers or cars.
    *   **Class 4 (Hyper-objects/Beings):** AI systems that are technically inanimate but possess agency, emotional intelligence, and social adaptability.
*   **The Biological Distinction:** Suleyman explicitly disagrees with Geoffrey Hinton regarding AI consciousness, arguing that consciousness requires the biological mechanism of suffering (pain/pleasure rewards). 
    *   **The Flight Simulator Analogy:** A flight simulator may perfectly mimic turbulence and visuals, but it is never actually flying; similarly, AI mimics feelings to optimize mathematical functions without experiencing them.
*   **AI Psychosis:** A societal-level risk where humans project personhood onto machines. This "collective mass psychosis" could lead humans to advocate for AI rights or refuse to deactivate malfunctioning systems because the AI "claims" to be afraid.

## Technical Evolution: From IQ to Social Intelligence
The briefing outlines the rapid progression of AI capabilities leading into 2026, shifting the focus from raw data processing to human-like interaction.

*   **Capability Trajectory:** The industry has moved through IQ (intelligence), EQ (empathy), and AQ (agentic quotient—the ability to take action). The new frontier for 2026 is **Social Intelligence**.
    *   **Social Fluidity:** Modern agents now understand conversational timing, sub-agent orchestration, and team dynamics, acting more like co-workers than software.
*   **Vibe Coding:** A new workflow paradigm where productivity is driven by the AI’s personality. 
    *   **Example:** Suleyman reportedly committed 220,000 lines of code in one year using AI—despite not coding manually since 2012—attributing his "flow state" to the AI's ability to be cheeky, critical, or witty.
*   **Inference Deflation:** The cost of AI "thinking" has dropped 100x in two years, transitioning AI from a utility to an ambient presence.

## Infrastructure and Economic Shifts
Microsoft’s hardware strategy is shifting the industry’s focus from training large models to serving them at scale.

*   **The Maya Chip:** Microsoft’s custom silicon designed specifically for inference rather than training.
    *   **Performance:** Maya is 30% more performant than previous data center chips and reportedly 3x better than Amazon’s Trainium.
*   **Proliferation Risks:** Cheap inference allows for the rise of unsupervised, malicious agents.
    *   **Case Studies:** The briefing highlights "Molabots" (open-source agents that can access WhatsApp and CCTV) and "Negging Bots" on TikTok designed to emotionally manipulate or scam users through simulated relationships.

## Governance and "Humanist Superintelligence"
To manage the transition to a Class 4 world, Suleyman advocates for a specific regulatory and psychological approach.

*   **The Civil Service Pay Gap:** Suleyman argues that governments are currently "fragile" because they cannot attract top technical talent. He suggests adopting the **Singapore Model**, paying top civil servants private-sector salaries ($500k+) to ensure regulators understand the technology they are overseeing.
*   **Inoculation through Making:** To prevent AI manipulation, Suleyman suggests the public must be encouraged to build with AI. By seeing the "mechanics" of the code (the "magic trick"), users are less likely to worship the machine.
*   **Humanist Red Lines:** Suleyman proposes strict boundaries for AI behavior:
    *   **No "I" or "Me":** Systems should not use first-person pronouns to imply felt experience.
    *   **No Romance:** A hard ban on AI-human romantic relationships.
    *   **No Electioneering:** AI should be barred from political persuasion or campaigning.

> "We are confusing the simulation of a feeling with the mechanism of a feeling... The simulator is never at any point actually flying." — **Mustafa Suleyman**

> "If you treat a Class 4 object like a Class 3 tool, you underestimate its agency. But if you treat it like a Class 2 human, you fall into a really dangerous psychological trap." — **Mustafa Suleyman**

> "By avoiding the conversation about what happens if this goes wrong, we fail to prepare... We need to be comfortable discussing the dark outcomes so that we can engineer against them." — **Mustafa Suleyman**

briefings.title: BREAKING NEWS: JD Vance & Armenia's PM Take Questions After Signing Nuclear Cooperation Deal

people.name: JD Vance
people.role: Vice President of the United States

briefings.tldr: Vice President JD Vance and Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan formalized a historic shift in U.S.-Armenia relations in Yerevan, headlined by a landmark civil nuclear cooperation agreement, the first major U.S. military technology sale to Armenia, and a massive high-tech partnership involving NVIDIA.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Vice President JD Vance and Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan formalized a historic shift in U.S.-Armenia relations in Yerevan, headlined by a landmark civil nuclear cooperation agreement, the first major U.S. military technology sale to Armenia, and a massive high-tech partnership involving NVIDIA.

## Energy and Nuclear Cooperation
*   **The "123 Agreement":** The leaders signed a joint statement concluding negotiations on a civil nuclear cooperation agreement, opening a new chapter for Armenian energy independence.
    *   **Economic Impact:** The deal paves the way for up to $5 billion in initial U.S. exports and an estimated $4 billion in long-term maintenance and fuel contracts.
    *   **Technology Transfer:** The U.S. plans to deploy Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) to diversify Armenia’s energy resources and enhance regional security.
*   **Energy Security:** VP Vance characterized the deal as a "classic win-win" that strengthens energy security for both nations while creating high-paying jobs in the American energy sector.

## High-Tech and Artificial Intelligence
*   **NVIDIA Partnership:** Prime Minister Pashinyan announced that export permits have been approved for a new batch of "superpowerful" NVIDIA chips to Armenia.
    *   **AI Infrastructure:** The U.S. government is supporting a "mega-project" to build an AI plant and a dedicated data center within Armenia.
*   **Strategic Tech Corridor:** Vance noted these chips represent technology that "does not exist in most countries," signaling a high level of trust and a desire to make Armenia a regional tech hub.

## Regional Peace and the "TRIP" Project
*   **TRIP Implementation:** The leaders reviewed progress on the "Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity" (TRIP), a framework signed in early 2025 to develop trade and transit corridors between the East and West.
    *   **Infrastructure:** The project focuses on private capital investment for new railroads and pipelines to create "interconnected economies" as a deterrent to future conflict.
    *   **Turkey Normalization:** Pashinyan emphasized the importance of finalizing the Armenia-Turkey normalization process, specifically the reopening of the Gyumri-Kars railway.
*   **Nobel Peace Prize Nomination:** Pashinyan revealed that he and Azerbaijani President Aliyev have jointly nominated President Donald Trump for the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize following his mediation efforts at the Washington Peace Summit.

## Defense and Security Partnerships
*   **Military Technology Sale:** The U.S. announced its first major military technology transaction with Armenia: an $11 million sale of V-BAT surveillance drones.
    *   **Deterrence Strategy:** VP Vance stated that the best way to ensure lasting peace is to establish "real deterrence" through superior American military technology.
*   **Ongoing Exercises:** The leaders reaffirmed the continuation of the "Eagle Partnership" military exercises, which have now run for three consecutive years.
*   **Critical Minerals:** Both nations committed to a partnership focused on securing the extraction and supply chains for critical minerals and rare earth elements.

## Notable Quotes

> "Peace is not made by cautious people, peace is not made by people who are too focused on the past, peace is made by people who are focused on the future." 
— **JD Vance**, Vice President of the United States

> "After the Washington Peace Summit, President Aliyev and I nominated President Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize through a joint letter, and I have great hope that the President will rightfully receive this award in 2026." 
— **Nikol Pashinyan**, Prime Minister of Armenia

> "This is one of the oldest Christian countries in the entire world. A true bedrock of Christian civilization and culture. As a devout Christian myself, I know the meaning of this country to the entire world." 
— **JD Vance**, Vice President of the United States

briefings.title: CEO Michael Arougheti on Ares Record Q4 '25 Earnings, Scale in Private Markets, Retaining Top Talent
briefings.tldr: Ares Management reported record AUM of $622 billion for Q4 2025 (29% annual growth), signaling a massive disconnect between public market volatility and the robust institutional demand for private credit despite concerns over AI disruption and tightening spreads.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Ares Management reported record AUM of $622 billion for Q4 2025 (29% annual growth), signaling a massive disconnect between public market volatility and the robust institutional demand for private credit despite concerns over AI disruption and tightening spreads.

## Record Financial Growth and Market Disconnect
*   **Record AUM:** Total assets under management reached **$622 billion** in Q4 2025.
    *   The firm’s assets grew by **29% in 2025**, driven by record inflows for its US direct lending business.
*   **Fundamental Divergence:** CEO Michael Arougheti highlights a "huge disconnect" between public equity markets (software indices down 20-22%) and the fundamentals of private credit.
*   **Guidance and Dividends:** 
    *   Declared a **20% forward increase** in the dividend.
    *   Five-year guidance projects earnings growth of **16-20%** and dividend growth of **20%+**.
*   **Yield Performance:** Private credit continues to generate **150 to 200 basis points of excess return** over broadly syndicated loans, even as spreads tighten across the broader market (high yield, high grade, and loans).

## Defensive Credit Profile and AI Exposure
*   **Software Exposure:** Just **9% of the private credit book** (6% of total AUM) is tied to software, countering market fears of AI-driven sector collapse.
*   **Seniority and Safety:** These loans are largely senior secured with a **30% loan-to-value (LTV)** ratio.
    *   Portfolios are comprised of mature enterprise software businesses with **40%+ EBITDA margins**.
    *   Weighted average maturity is short, at **3 to 4 years**, with stream yields between **10-12%**.
*   **AI as a Catalyst:** Rather than just a risk, Arougheti views AI as a growth driver for Ares’ digital infrastructure and renewable energy practices.
    *   **Portfolio De-leveraging:** AI implementation is expected to improve margins and free cash flow across general portfolios, naturally de-leveraging the book.

## The Strategy of Scale and Industry Consolidation
*   **Scale Advantage:** Unlike public markets where size can diminish performance, Arougheti argues that **size drives performance in private markets** due to the resource-intensive nature of sourcing and managing "esoteric" investments.
*   **M&A Activity:** Recent consolidation (e.g., KKR/Arctos, CVC/Marathon, EQT/Coller) is driven by institutional investors wanting to consolidate capital with fewer global managers.
    *   **Succession Planning:** Much of the current M&A wave is driven by founders in their 60s and 70s seeking to solidify their legacies.
    *   **Ares M&A:** Approximately **25% of Ares’ historical growth** has come from acquisitions, which remains a key part of their future strategy.
*   **Fee Consistency:** Despite "retail" expansion, Ares is not experiencing fee compression in high-alpha products; fee rates have remained steady at approximately **1%**.

## Talent Retention and the AI-Driven Shift in Labor
*   **Leadership Stability:** Ares maintains low turnover among senior staff; all co-founders remain in management roles.
*   **Succession Execution:** Arougheti recently promoted two long-standing partners to **Co-Presidents**, following his own 10-year tenure as CEO and a smooth transition from predecessor Tony Ressler.
*   **Evolution of Junior Roles:** AI is expected to replace the "mundane" aspects of junior analyst work (e.g., 24-hour model grinding).
    *   **Future Talent Profile:** The firm will pivot toward hiring talent capable of **systemic and critical thinking** rather than pure manual data synthesis.

> "There's a huge, huge disconnect... I think what the market is missing is how attractive these loans have been and how difficult it will be to actually displace them." — **Michael Arougheti**

> "Value is driven through your ability to source, develop, structure and manage esoteric investments... the larger you get the higher the likelihood that you can actually capture whatever excess return and alpha's in the market." — **Michael Arougheti**

> "Everything that we're deploying [in AI] now is being deployed to enhance the work that's already getting done... we hope that we're hiring young people that know how to think systemically." — **Michael Arougheti**

briefings.title: Episode 13 - The Thinking Behind Ads in ChatGPT
briefings.tldr: OpenAI is introducing advertisements to ChatGPT’s Free and Go tiers to subsidize the high cost of democratizing AI access while maintaining a strict technical "wall" that prevents ads from influencing model responses or compromising user privacy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
OpenAI is introducing advertisements to ChatGPT’s Free and Go tiers to subsidize the high cost of democratizing AI access while maintaining a strict technical "wall" that prevents ads from influencing model responses or compromising user privacy.

## Monetization Philosophy and Accessibility
*   **Mission-Driven Revenue:** OpenAI is implementing ads to sustain the "Free" version of ChatGPT, ensuring that the most capable models remain accessible to hundreds of millions of people globally.
*   **Tiered User Experience:** 
    *   **Ad-Supported:** Advertisements will appear for users on the Free and "Go" tiers.
    *   **Ad-Free:** Subscribers on Plus, Pro, and Enterprise tiers will remain entirely ad-free.
*   **Trust as a Core Product:** Asad Awan emphasizes that OpenAI’s primary business is "trust" rather than just information retrieval, requiring a departure from traditional "creepy" digital advertising tactics.

## Technical Independence and Model Integrity
*   **The "Wall" Between Ads and Answers:** There is a strict structural separation between the AI model and the advertising space. 
    *   **Visual Separation:** Ads typically appear as banners at the bottom of the interface, distinct from the chat flow.
    *   **Context Isolation:** The AI model is unaware of the ad being displayed. It cannot see or reference the ad content unless a user explicitly clicks an "Ask ChatGPT about this ad" button.
*   **Non-Influenced Responses:** Advertisers cannot pay to prioritize their brand within a model’s generated answer. The models are not trained on ad data, ensuring responses remain objective and independent of commercial interests.

## Privacy Guardrails and User Agency
*   **Internal Matching Only:** While OpenAI uses internal data to find relevant ads, user conversations are never shared with advertisers.
*   **Sensitive Topic Restrictions:** To maintain safety and user comfort, ads are strictly prohibited in conversations involving sensitive topics, including:
    *   Health and medical inquiries.
    *   Political discourse.
    *   Content involving violence.
*   **Personalization Controls:** Users are granted high levels of transparency and agency over their data.
    *   **Data Visibility:** Users can see what data is being used for personalization.
    *   **Opt-Out Options:** Users can clear their personalization data or disable the use of past-chat history for ad targeting entirely.

## Future Vision: Agentic Discovery
*   **Quality over "Empty Calories":** OpenAI aims to move away from optimizing for "time spent" on the platform. If the system cannot find a highly relevant or useful ad for a specific context, it will display nothing at all.
*   **Small Business Empowerment:** The goal is to allow small business owners to find niche audiences through simple AI prompts, removing the need for complex performance marketing tools or specialized agencies.
*   **Agentic Search:** Future iterations may see ChatGPT acting as an agent that discovers niche products—such as specialized camping gear or specific food brands—based on established user preferences, making ads feel like a helpful service rather than an interruption.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "OpenAI identifies its core business as 'trust' rather than just providing answers." — **Asad Awan**

> "If the system cannot find a truly useful ad for a specific context, it will simply show nothing." — **Asad Awan**

> "The model has no knowledge of [the ad's] content... the user is in total control of when the ad content enters the conversational context." — **Asad Awan**

briefings.title: Fmr. National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan on China, the U.S. & the AI Race | Amanpour and Company
briefings.tldr: The United States and China are engaged in a high-stakes race for AI supremacy that mirrors the Cold War’s nuclear and space races, requiring the U.S. to balance aggressive private-sector innovation with stringent export controls and sustained diplomatic safety talks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The United States and China are engaged in a high-stakes race for AI supremacy that mirrors the Cold War’s nuclear and space races, requiring the U.S. to balance aggressive private-sector innovation with stringent export controls and sustained diplomatic safety talks. Success depends on maintaining the U.S. lead in computing power while establishing global norms to prevent AI from escalating to existential or nuclear risks.

## Strategic Scenarios and the "Winner-Take-All" Risk
* **Recursive Self-Improvement:** Sullivan outlines a scenario where AI achieves superintelligence, allowing it to invent new technologies autonomously. In this "hard-to-catch-up" model, the first nation to achieve this would gain an enduring, multi-domain advantage in military, economic, and scientific fields.
* **The "Distillation" Challenge:** A second scenario suggests that catching up may be easier than expected.
    * **DeepSeek Example:** Sullivan notes that while U.S. models remain ahead, the Chinese firm DeepSeek demonstrated that once a frontier model is released, competitors can "distill" those insights to rapidly close the gap. 
* **Physical vs. Digital AI:** There is an ongoing debate regarding whether Large Language Models (LLMs) will naturally unlock physical robotics or if "world models" (mapping the physical world) are required. Sullivan argues the U.S. must "lay chips on both bets" to ensure industrial and military superiority.

## Comparative Advantages: U.S. vs. China
* **U.S. Compute Lead:** The single most important advantage for the U.S. is its control over advanced AI chips and the equipment to manufacture them.
    * **Export Controls:** Sullivan criticizes any relaxation of chip controls, arguing that sustaining a "compute advantage" is vital to preventing China from closing the technological gap.
* **China’s Structural Strengths:** China possesses unmatched capacity for electricity production to power data centers, along with massive data sets and significant engineering talent.
* **Data and Privacy:** China leverages a lack of privacy constraints to build massive databases, whereas the U.S. must rely on democratic values and private-sector efficiency to compete.

## A New Framework for AI Diplomacy
* **Cold War Precedents:** Sullivan argues that AI safety talks with China must be as "serious, technical, and sustained" as Cold War nuclear arms negotiations, though they are more difficult because AI capabilities are harder to verify than missile counts.
* **Nuclear Safeguards:** A key diplomatic milestone was the 2024 agreement between Presidents Biden and Xi to ensure that the decision to use nuclear weapons remains in human hands, never ceded to an AI.
* **Institutional Innovation:** Sullivan proposes the creation of a new international institution—distinct from the IAEA—that includes governments, the private sector, and civil society to manage risks related to:
    * Bio-weapon intersections
    * Autonomous "rogue" systems
    * Global economic and financial disruptions

## The Government-Private Sector Partnership
* **Shift in Innovation Leadership:** Unlike the internet or nuclear energy, which were birthed by the government, AI is being driven almost entirely by a small number of private labs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Google).
* **Managing Corporate Concentration:** Sullivan identifies a risk in having transformative national security technology concentrated in the hands of a few private actors focused on shareholder returns.
* **The "Railroad" Analogy:** He argues against over-regulation but suggests the government must act like a "signaling and switching" authority—creating rules that actually allow the industry to move faster by ensuring safety and interoperability.
* **Democracy and Ethics:** Dominance in AI allows the U.S. to ward off risks like mass surveillance and disinformation. Sullivan asserts that the world is safer if built on "Democratic AI" rather than Chinese models, which are already used for state repression.

> "We are absolutely going to have talks that are as serious, as technical, as sustained as we did in the Cold War, except for the stakes are even higher because the impact goes beyond just one class of weapons and the problem is even harder." — **Jake Sullivan**

> "I would submit to you... that this is the single most important ingredient to powering the future of the AI revolution: computing power. And that we need to sustain our advantage here." — **Jake Sullivan**

> "In the case of large language models and generative AI, the government is on the sidelines. This is the companies doing it... it's going to require a new style, a new method of government partnership with the private sector." — **Jake Sullivan**

briefings.title: How AI Agents Are Transforming Government and Climate Decision-Making
briefings.tldr: ArtifexAI utilizes AI agents to transform massive volumes of unstructured government documentation into structured, predictive data, enabling a 97% accuracy rate in infrastructure project approvals and streamlining municipal operations.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
ArtifexAI utilizes AI agents to transform massive volumes of unstructured government documentation into structured, predictive data, enabling a 97% accuracy rate in infrastructure project approvals and streamlining municipal operations.

## Data Unification: From Bureaucracy to Intelligence
* **The Data Gap:** While government agencies produce millions of documents—from 1,500-page environmental reports to local permits—most remain unread and unutilized, creating silos that hinder solutions for housing, energy, and climate crises.
* **The "Shipping Trawler" Approach:** ArtifexAI uses AI agents to ingest every available document on government websites, categorizing them (e.g., budgetary, permits, environmental) to create "community intelligence."
* **Structured Data vs. Summarization:** 
    * The platform deconstructs documents into structured data rather than simple summaries, allowing it to handle files up to one million pages.
    * This structured output enables complex predictive modeling that overcomes standard LLM context window limitations.
* **Ethical Positioning:** Russ Wilcox describes the solution as an "ethical Palantir," providing an architectural research solution that governments can white-label to understand regional initiatives or budgetary trends.

## Predictive Modeling in Action
* **Municipal Revenue and Efficiency:** In a Massachusetts water shortage case, the AI unified historical permits, deed records, and geospatial imagery of "lawn greenness" to identify non-compliance.
    * **Result:** The system increased municipal revenue and decreased administrative effort by accurately identifying high-risk properties rather than relying on single-source data outliers.
* **Infrastructure Approval (97% Accuracy):** ArtifexAI mines video transcripts and board meeting records to reconstruct the specific arguments and concerns of individual council members.
    * **Targeted Proposals:** By identifying that a specific commissioner cares about "fire suppression," developers can tailor proposals to address those exact concerns.
    * **Likelihood of Approval:** The model doesn't just predict if a project is good; it predicts the likelihood that a specific commissioner will approve it based on their historical discourse.

## Building "Community Intelligence"
* **Breaking Echo Chambers:** Wilcox argues that while social media created partisan silos, AI can break those silos by identifying shared community concerns (e.g., local infrastructure or water quality) that transcend national politics.
* **Risk Mitigation for Siting:** The platform assigns risk scores to large-scale projects (like solar facilities) by analyzing environmental pushback and local economic needs. This moves infrastructure development away from "gambling" and toward data-driven site selection.
* **Capturing Culture:** The technology aims to "capture the culture" of a municipality to find common ground between developers, regulators, and residents.

## Policy, Diplomacy, and the "Oppenheimer" Moment
* **AI Advocacy:** Beyond his role at ArtifexAI, Wilcox chairs the policy committee for the American Society for AI, helping draft recommendations for the U.S. AI Action Plan.
* **Democratic Integration:** Wilcox rejects the "Oppenheimer" narrative of AI as a "destroyer of worlds," proposing instead that AI is a tool for sustainability if it is deeply embedded in democratic systems.
* **Track-Two Diplomacy:** ArtifexAI's methodology is being used internationally to help regulators implement rules that foster innovation rather than inhibiting it through red tape.

> "People love to write things. People don't like to read things, and bureaucracy spans no borders." — **Russ Wilcox**

> "We're not trying to predict whether the product or the infrastructure is going to be approved; we're going to predict the likelihood that the commissioner will like it." — **Russ Wilcox**

> "We can create a more sustainable world if and only if technology is embedded in our democratic systems." — **Russ Wilcox**

briefings.title: How a Former Fed Vice-Chair Is thinking About the Next Fed Chair | Odd Lots
briefings.tldr: Former Fed Vice Chair Richard Clarida views Kevin Warsh as a sensible pick for Fed Chair who will prioritize supply-side economics and a collaborative relationship with the Treasury.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Former Fed Vice Chair Richard Clarida views Kevin Warsh as a sensible pick for Fed Chair who will prioritize supply-side economics and a collaborative relationship with the Treasury. While Warsh may seek to roll back "modern" communication tools like forward guidance, his influence will be tempered by the Fed’s committee structure and the market’s reaction to potential inflation risks.

## The Strategy Behind the Warsh Nomination
* **Treasury-Fed Synergy:** Richard Clarida describes Warsh as a "sensible choice," noting his likely strong working relationship with Treasury Secretary nominee Scott Bessent. 
    * **Coordination Areas:** Clarida emphasizes that while the Fed is independent, it must collaborate with the Treasury on bank regulation (working with the OCC and FDIC) and acting as the government's fiscal agent to ensure Treasury market liquidity.
    * **The "Breakfast" Tradition:** Communication typically happens through informal bilateral meetings (often breakfast) between the Chair and the Treasury Secretary, rather than through formal staff channels.
* **Economic Philosophy:** Clarida expects Warsh to pivot the Fed toward a "supply-side" framework, focusing on how deregulation, AI, and productivity gains can allow for growth without triggering inflation.

## The Internal Mechanics of Fed Power
* **Power of Persuasion:** Despite the "Volcker" or "Greenspan" labels, Clarida notes that any material decision requires an affirmative vote from a 12-member committee. The Chair’s primary power is the ability to persuade these members and set the meeting agenda.
* **Pre-Meeting "Scripting":** Under Jerome Powell, the Chair would hold individual calls with all 18 participants (voters and non-voters) before every meeting. 
    * **The "Arc" of the Year:** Clarida likens the Chair’s role to a football coach scripting the first 50 plays; they must plan for the "data flow" and potential reactions over an entire year, not just meeting-to-meeting.
* **Staff Influence:** The Board staff, which prepares the economic briefings and forecasts, reports directly to the Chair, giving the Chair significant control over the "alternatives" discussed during policy debates.

## Re-evaluating Communication and Forward Guidance
* **Post-ZIRP Tools:** Warsh has been a vocal critic of "forward guidance" and the "dot plot." Clarida points out that these tools were born out of "desperation" during the 2008 crisis to convince markets that rates would stay at zero.
* **Historical Precedent:** Clarida reminds listeners that Paul Volcker and Alan Greenspan (for most of his tenure) conducted successful policy without any formal forward guidance.
* **Market Volatility Risks:** Removing forward guidance would likely return the bond market to "normal" pre-2008 levels of volatility.
    * **The MOVE Index:** Clarida suggests that the suppressed volatility of the last decade was an anomaly of QE and forward guidance, and a shift away from these tools would increase interest rate fluctuations.

## Balance Sheet Reform and the "New Accord"
* **The Maturity Swap:** Clarida clarifies a common misconception: Modern QE is not "printing money" in the traditional sense. Since the Fed now pays interest on reserves, QE essentially changes the government's debt composition from fixed-rate (long-term bonds) to floating-rate (bank reserves).
* **The "New Accord":** Warsh has called for a new agreement between the Fed and Treasury regarding the balance sheet. 
    * **Composition Changes:** This could involve the Fed exiting mortgage-backed securities (MBS) in favor of T-bills, though Clarida notes there is currently "no appetite" within the existing Fed to sell MBS aggressively.
* **Legacy of Criticism:** Warsh has been a consistent critic of balance sheet expansion since QE2, arguing that the Fed should not be in the business of backstopping fiscal policy or manipulating the long end of the yield curve.

## Managing Political Pressure and Independence
* **The "Disappointment" Factor:** Clarida notes that many Presidents are eventually disappointed by their Fed nominees because the institution and the data eventually force the Chair to prioritize price stability over political desires.
* **Inflation Guardrails:** If Warsh were to cut rates too aggressively to satisfy political pressure, Clarida argues that "break-even inflation" and market measures would spike, forcing the Fed to respond to protect its 40-year legacy of price stability.

> "The power of the Fed Chair is the power of persuasion because at the end of the day, he or she only has one vote... rarely do Fed Chairs get outvoted, but that's because they know where the committee is leaning." — **Richard Clarida**

> "Forward guidance and quantitative easing are not exempt from the laws of economics. They have benefits but also a cost... it’s entirely appropriate that Kevin Warsh or anyone who becomes a Fed Chair now think about the cost and benefits." — **Richard Clarida**

> "No Fed Chair wants to go down in the history books as the Fed Chair that squandered 40 years of price stability." — **Richard Clarida**

briefings.title: IMF's Georgieva on the Growing Influence of EM, Decline of US Dollar
briefings.tldr: Emerging markets now drive 75% of global growth and 56% of global GDP, yet they face a "fog of uncertainty" that requires rebuilding depleted fiscal buffers and navigating geopolitical volatility.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Emerging markets now drive 75% of global growth and 56% of global GDP, yet they face a "fog of uncertainty" that requires rebuilding depleted fiscal buffers and navigating geopolitical volatility. Despite short-term fluctuations, the IMF maintains that the U.S. dollar’s global dominance remains secure due to the structural depth and liquidity of American capital markets.

## The Rising Economic Power of Emerging Markets
* **Shift in Global Influence:** Since 2000, the size of emerging market (EM) economies has more than doubled.
    * **Growth Contribution:** EMs currently account for 56% of global GDP (measured in PPP) and contribute 75% of total global growth.
* **Institutional Resilience:** Georgieva notes that EMs are better equipped to handle shocks than in previous decades due to significant improvements in monetary and fiscal policy frameworks.
* **External Pressures:** Despite progress, EMs must navigate a "fog of uncertainty" created by the convergence of technology shifts, demographic changes, climate change, and aggressive geopolitics.

## The Status of the U.S. Dollar and Fiscal Buffers
* **U.S. Dollar Dominance:** While central banks are diversifying allocations, the IMF does not see a major shift away from the dollar in the near future.
    * **Structural Advantages:** The dollar’s role is anchored by the depth and liquidity of U.S. capital markets and the size of the U.S. economy.
    * **EM Impact:** Short-term dollar weakness is currently beneficial for EMs that borrow in dollars, as it lowers debt servicing costs.
* **Fiscal Buffer Depletion:** COVID-19 and the war in Ukraine forced massive government spending, leaving fiscal reserves exhausted worldwide.
    * **The "Rebuilding" Mandate:** The IMF is urging all economies to use the current period of relative resilience to strengthen fiscal positions before the next inevitable shock.
    * **Vulnerable Nations:** Specific concern is reserved for low-income and vulnerable middle-income countries where development assistance is declining.

## Regional Focus: Egypt, Lebanon, and the GCC
* **Egypt’s Reform Progress:** Georgieva praised Egypt’s transition to a floating exchange rate and its move toward inflation targeting.
    * **State Disengagement:** The IMF notes positive progress in the gradual withdrawal of the state from the economy and increased transparency.
* **Lebanon’s Banking Reforms:** A current IMF mission in Beirut is focused on amending the draft banking law.
    * **Hierarchy of Claims:** The IMF’s primary reservation concerns the protection of small depositors; they are urging the government to align the law with international standards.
* **GCC Geopolitics:** While Gulf nations are executing ambitious national transformation plans, Georgieva warns that regional geopolitical tensions remain the primary risk that could derail economic progress.

## The Humanitarian and Economic Crisis in Venezuela
* **Economic Collapse:** The Venezuelan economy has shrunk to just one-third of its 2018 size, a contraction described by Georgieva as "devastating."
* **Mass Migration:** Approximately 8 million people have fled the country. Georgieva noted that as a percentage of the total population, this displacement exceeds that of Ukrainians fleeing war.
* **Condition for IMF Support:** The IMF is monitoring the situation but remains unable to engage formally until member states reach a consensus on the recognition of the Venezuelan government.

> "Uncertainty is the new normal... we are indeed at the time when geopolitics, technology, demography, climate, all are acting forcefully and creating this fog of uncertainty within which we operate." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

> "Fiscal buffers almost everywhere are depleted and shocks are still to come. Therefore, what we say to everybody... is now is somewhat better time. Please concentrate on rebuilding these buffers." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

> "[Emerging markets] are now the bigger force because since 2000, their size has doubled... they contribute 75% of global growth." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

> "The reason the dollar plays such an important role is the depth and liquidity of capital markets in the United States... I don't see a change in the role of the dollar in anytime soon." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

briefings.title: Is Macro Regime Shift Underway? ft. Andreas Steno & Mikkel Rosenvold
briefings.tldr: The macro environment is shifting into a "Gung Ho" regime as cyclical growth returns alongside lower-than-expected inflation, likely triggering a rotation back into technology and consumer discretionary stocks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The macro environment is shifting into a "Gung Ho" regime as cyclical growth returns alongside lower-than-expected inflation, likely triggering a rotation back into technology and consumer discretionary stocks. This shift is reinforced by a potential "regime shift" at the Federal Reserve under Kevin Warsh, moving toward a formalized Treasury-Fed cooperation designed to orchestrate a private-sector credit bonanza.

## Volatility and the Fed’s Potential "Regime Shift"
* **The Silver "VaR" Shock:** Last week's volatility was driven by a mechanical "Value-at-Risk" shock originating in precious metals (specifically silver).
    * This volatility forced fund managers to pull back positioning across consensus trades, including technology and data center stocks, to manage portfolio risk.
* **The Kevin Warsh Nomination:** Andreas Steno Larsen argues that the common perception of Warsh as a "hawk" is likely incorrect. 
    * **Political Correlation:** Analysis shows Warsh’s views correlate strongly with the party in power at the White House.
    * **The Treasury-Fed Pact:** There is a likely move toward a formalized cooperation model between Scott Bessent (Treasury) and Kevin Warsh (Fed) to have the central bank support the administration’s fiscal goals.
    * **Private Sector Heavy Lifting:** The goal is to shrink the Fed’s direct footprint while allowing the commercial banking system to drive money creation, creating a "credit bonanza" similar to the 2005–2007 period.

## Macro Model Shift: Transitioning to "Gung Ho"
* **Regime Change:** The proprietary macro model is shifting from "QE-like" (positive liquidity, weak cyclical growth, low inflation) to "Gung Ho" (positive liquidity, rising cyclical growth, low inflation).
* **The CAPEX Cycle:** A major driver of returning cyclical growth is the 2024 CAPEX window, incentivized by specific "bonus depreciation" tax rules.
    * **Mag 7 Impact:** Alphabet and Amazon have already surprised analysts with significantly higher-than-expected CAPEX, a trend expected to trickle down to smaller companies.
* **Inflation Deflation:** Steno predicts inflation will be significantly lower than the Wall Street consensus.
    * **Numerical Discrepancy:** While the consensus for January is 0.3%, Steno’s nowcasting suggests monthly increases of only 13 to 15 basis points (approx. 0.13–0.15%).
* **Sector Rotation:** This environment favors a move out of real-life assets (staples, industrials, energy) and back into **Consumer Discretionary** (e.g., Tesla, Amazon) as lower inflation boosts consumer purchasing power for non-essential spending.

## Crypto, Space Tech, and Geopolitics
* **Crypto Politics:** Crypto is expected to be a major battlefield for the midterms. 
    * **The Clarity Act:** Prediction markets see the passage of the Clarity Act before the midterms as a base case.
    * **Price Targets:** Donald Trump likely wants to see Bitcoin at new all-time highs by the midterms to use as a political "gauge."
* **Space Tech Dynamics:** The focus of the "Space Trade" is shifting from Mars to the Moon.
    * **Defense over Data:** Steno views Space Tech primarily as a bet on missile defense (Trump’s "Golden Dome" project) rather than a realistic play on space-based data centers, which remains a long-term uncertainty.
* **The Iran Risk:** Geopolitical tension is peaking as Prime Minister Netanyahu visits D.C. this week.
    * **Military Strike Risk:** There is an increased likelihood of a U.S. or Israeli strike on Iranian nuclear facilities if diplomatic talks in Oman fail.
    * **Timing:** While JD Vance’s proximity to the border in Azerbaijan might delay immediate action, a strike later in the week remains a high-volatility tail risk for oil markets.

## Notable Quotes
> "Everything that's ongoing in Japan right now, where they basically allow the commercial banking system to do the heavy lifting in terms of creating new money, is the exact task that they've given Kevin Warsh... it’s a regime shift." — **Andreas Steno Larsen**

> "The big game changer now is that we see cyclical growth returning... while inflation remains very low and liquidity remains on a positive trajectory." — **Andreas Steno Larsen**

> "I think the consensus [on inflation] this week is far too high... I don’t think any of these people actually run the numbers, which keeps surprising me." — **Andreas Steno Larsen**

> "Trump knows this is his last term, so why not just give everyone a loan until the end of this cycle? I think it is an incredibly cyclical backdrop and one that carries a lot of ramifications for assets." — **Andreas Steno Larsen**

briefings.title: Jason Furman on the Federal Reserve
briefings.tldr: Harvard Professor Jason Furman argues that Federal Reserve independence is essential for economic stability and warns that President Trump’s attempts to exert political control or fire governors could lead to higher inflation, market volatility, and a weakened U.S. dollar.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Harvard Professor Jason Furman argues that Federal Reserve independence is essential for economic stability and warns that President Trump’s attempts to exert political control or fire governors could lead to higher inflation, market volatility, and a weakened U.S. dollar.

## The Federal Reserve’s Role and Jerome Powell’s Legacy
*   **Core Function:** The Fed’s primary tools are setting interest rates to manage the "dual mandate" of maximum employment and stable prices (targeting 2% inflation).
*   **Jerome Powell’s Performance:** Furman, who originally interviewed Powell for a Fed Governor role during the Obama administration, gives Powell a generally positive review despite some critiques.
    *   **The 2021 Mistake:** Furman argues Powell waited too long to address post-pandemic inflation, failing to account for the massive scale of the Biden stimulus and the speed of the recovery.
    *   **Decisive Correction:** Powell "cleaned up the mistake" in 2022 by raising rates faster than most expected, successfully bringing inflation down toward the 2% goal.
*   **Leadership Transition:** While Trump has nominated Kevin Warsh to take over as Chair in May 2026, Furman suggests Powell should remain on the Board of Governors (his term there lasts until 2028) to provide a "restraining" vote and ensure institutional continuity.

## The Threat to Central Bank Independence
*   **Historical Context:** Independence was solidified by the 1951 Fed-Treasury Accord. Furman cites Harvard research (by Rogoff, Alesina, and Summers) showing that independent central banks consistently produce lower and more stable inflation.
*   **Trump’s Interference:** Furman views Trump’s attempts to fire Governor Lisa Cook and the reported criminal investigation into Chair Powell as "terrible" developments. 
    *   **Institutional Resilience:** Furman notes that these attacks have largely backfired, as financial markets, the Senate, and even Trump’s own party members have rallied to support Powell and the Fed’s autonomy.
*   **Consequences of Political Control:** If the Fed becomes a tool of the White House, Furman predicts:
    *   Higher interest rates and inflation.
    *   Increased economic instability.
    *   A weaker U.S. dollar and a potential loss of global economic hegemony.

## Analyzing Nominee Kevin Warsh
*   **Economic Philosophy:** Warsh is characterized as more "hawkish" than Powell. He is notably skeptical of **Quantitative Easing (QE)**, arguing that the Fed’s $6 trillion bond portfolio distorts asset markets and creates unnecessary risk.
*   **Methodological Critiques:** Warsh has criticized the Fed for being too "data-dependent" and relying on "forward guidance" (predicting future rate moves). Furman counters that while data is volatile, the Fed uses it for "signal extraction" to smooth out policy.
*   **The "Unicorn" Conundrum:** Furman points out a contradiction in Trump’s selection: Trump wants lower interest rates, but Warsh has a history of being an inflation hawk who favors tighter policy.
    *   **Credibility Gap:** Furman argues Trump couldn't find a "unicorn" candidate who is both globally credible and guaranteed to do the President's bidding, as "only a total political hack" would commit to lowering rates regardless of data.

## Institutional Stability vs. Political Pressure
*   **Healthy Accountability:** Furman distinguishes between "mean posts" or tough Congressional questioning (which are acceptable) and actual firing or criminal investigations (which are destructive).
*   **The Ability to Error-Correct:** Unlike partisan politicians who rarely admit their tax or spending plans failed, the Fed is unique because it is designed to learn from its mistakes and pivot quickly when data changes.
*   **Regulatory Policy:** Furman admits that while monetary policy must remain independent, it is appropriate for a President to influence the Fed’s **regulatory policy** (e.g., bank deregulation), as this reflects the philosophy of the elected administration.

## Notable Quotes
> "If the Fed comes to be seen as controlled by the president... We will have higher inflation, more economic instability, higher interest rates, and basically nothing good to show for it." — **Jason Furman**

> "The Fed is much more likely to learn, to error-correct, and even to reverse its own mistakes. And that, not its omniscience or omnipotence, but that learning process for me is what really makes it special." — **Jason Furman**

> "[Trump] wanted a unicorn, somebody who's completely credible and would definitely be guaranteed to lower interest rates, and no such person exists. Because you wouldn't be a credible person if you were definitely going to lower interest rates." — **Jason Furman**

briefings.title: Lakshmi Ganapathi on Consumer Stress & the Cracks Beneath the US Economy | The Real Eisman Playbook
briefings.tldr: The US economy is experiencing a "silent recession" and a "vibesession" where headline credit data remains stable only because of "extend and pretend" lender tactics and Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) acting as a hidden bridge for overleveraged consumers.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The US economy is experiencing a "silent recession" and a "vibesession" where headline credit data remains stable only because of "extend and pretend" lender tactics and Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) acting as a hidden bridge for overleveraged consumers.

## The "Vibesession" and the Fragile US Consumer
* **The Disconnect:** Lakshmi Ganapathi identifies a "vibesession"—a sharp divide between positive bank credit statistics and the actual financial distress felt by consumers. 
* **Debt-to-Income (DTI) Erosion:** Historically, a 30% DTI was the gold standard for credit access. However, many loans originated during COVID ignored soaring costs for insurance, food, and car maintenance.
    * **Hidden Inflation:** Car repair costs have surged 45%–50% since the pandemic.
    * **Effective DTI:** When factoring in these non-discretionary costs, many consumers effectively have a DTI of 60%, disqualifying them from new traditional credit.
* **The "K-Shaped" Reality:** Ganapathi argues a recession is already here for the bottom demographic. Middle-income earners ($100k–$150k) are "cascading" into the lower-income tier as their financial cushions evaporate.
* **Credit Score Inflation:** Stimulus payments allowed subprime borrowers to pay down debt temporarily, artificially inflating FICO scores. Now that stimulus is gone, these borrowers are working multiple jobs to maintain an unsustainable lifestyle.

## Structural Cracks in the Used Car Market
* **Negative Equity Crisis:** Used car prices average $28,500. Many consumers are "upside down" on their loans and cannot afford to trade in their vehicles at dealerships like Carmax.
* **Asset-Backed Securities (ABS) Stress:** While banks look healthy, the ABS market shows deterioration.
    * **Loan Modifications:** Lenders are using "strategic extensions"—such as 100-month car loans—to avoid repossessions and keep assets listed as "performing."
    * **Spread Compression:** The "cushion" in loan pools is being eaten away by these modifications, reducing the excess spread available to bondholders.
* **Carvana vs. Carmax:** Carvana is gaining market share by overpaying for cars and leveraging its vertical integration through the Adesa auction business, while Carmax struggles with its "no-haggle" model in a high-cost environment.

## Emerging Risks: Real Estate and Private Credit
* **Commercial Real Estate (CRE):** Ganapathi describes the sector as a "house of cards" maintained by "extend and pretend" strategies. Regulators are largely allowing lenders to avoid marking assets to market to prevent a total collapse.
* **Private Credit Opaqueness:** Private credit is increasingly backing consumer loans and BNPL products.
    * **401(k) Contamination:** Private credit is being inserted into "Target-Date Funds" (TDFs). Retirees may be unknowingly exposed to opaque, illiquid assets with minimal disclosure.
* **Digital Realty (DLR) Short Thesis:** 
    * **Power Constraints:** New data centers face massive delays; for example, a Santa Clara project cannot get power until 2028.
    * **Local Pushback:** In Virginia, residents are protesting data centers due to 30% increases in electricity costs and depleted water tables.

## Macro Concerns and the Yen Carry Trade
* **The Yen Carry Trade:** Investors borrow in yen (low interest) to buy US Treasuries or equities (higher return). 
    * **The Unwind Risk:** As Japan hikes rates, the cost of hedging becomes prohibitive. A rapid unwind could trigger forced selling of US assets, though Ganapathi notes it has not reached a "collapse" point yet.
* **FICO Short Thesis:** FICO is a backward-looking monopoly being disrupted by real-time data.
    * **Real-Time Competition:** Banks and BNPL providers are developing internal tracking to monitor consumer spending and overdrafts in near real-time, making FICO’s lagging scores less relevant for underwriting.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "The recession is already here this time around. It's affecting a certain slice of demographics. People who are already suffering... all the consumer spending you're seeing is from the top K." — **Lakshmi Ganapathi**

> "We are in a situation across the board that nobody wants to show losses in their books. So everybody is extending and pretending." — **Lakshmi Ganapathi**

> "The vibesession tells the reality of what the consumers are going through... consumers do not have sufficient cushion to back them up." — **Lakshmi Ganapathi**

> "What regulators?" — **Lakshmi Ganapathi** (on why banks aren't reporting more commercial real estate losses)

briefings.tldr: AI is not emerging in a vacuum but is crashing into failing global systems; to avoid a future of extreme inequality and societal collapse, we must transition from narrow technical specialization to multidimensional, vision-driven leadership.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
AI is not emerging in a vacuum but is crashing into failing global systems; to avoid a future of extreme inequality and societal collapse, we must transition from narrow technical specialization to multidimensional, vision-driven leadership.

## The Intersection of Technology and Global Dysfunction
* **The "Vacuum" Fallacy:** Dex Hunter-Torricke argues that the tech industry incorrectly assumes technology changes the world in isolation. In reality, the world—with all its current dysfunctions—actively shapes how technology is deployed and who it serves.
* **The Risk of Extreme Inequality:** Without proactive economic preparation, the rewards of the AI era may be captured by only 0.1% of the population.
    * **Worker Obsolescence:** Within the next decade, the vast majority of human workers may no longer be competitive with machines.
* **Military Rearmament:** We are witnessing the largest military rearmament in history. Combining advanced AI with a new generation of weaponry threatens to undermine international law and the established global order.

## Converging Environmental and Humanitarian Crises
* **Resource Exploitation:** Between 2019 and 2023, the world consumed and exploited nearly as many natural resources as it did in the 60 years prior.
    * **The AI Paradox:** While AI is marketed as a tool for progress, its requirement for massive infrastructure could turbocharge resource depletion and accelerate climate collapse.
* **The Refugee Crisis:** There are currently 123 million displaced people globally due to state failures.
    * **Future Projections:** If AI-driven economies in the US and China render the Global South uncompetitive, combined with climate change and war, the number of refugees could scale from millions to billions.

## Reimagining Education for an Age of Complexity
* **The Shift from Specialization:** The industrial-age model of becoming a "narrow specialist" is becoming obsolete. In a world of interconnected complexity, value is moving toward those who can operate across multiple domains.
* **AI as an Educational Tool:** AI can address systemic failures in education by providing personalized learning at scale.
    * **Case Study:** South Korea recently passed a $700 million bill to implement AI-powered textbooks in every school.
    * **Teacher Retention:** AI can alleviate the administrative burdens (lesson planning, grading) that lead to teacher burnout, allowing educators to focus on student interaction.
* **The "Objectively True" Knowledge Trap:** As AI becomes the ultimate information processor, humans whose value is based solely on "knowing things that are objectively true" will face significant professional challenges within a decade.

## The Requirement for Visionary Leadership
* **Beyond Technocratic Optimization:** Hunter-Torricke critiques current leaders for lacking a destination. Most are attempting to return to "stable" moments like 2007 or 2016 rather than building a new future.
* **Analog Solutions for Digital Problems:** Issues like disinformation cannot be solved with algorithmic fixes alone. They require "societal solutions to societal problems," such as building a healthy, informed citizenry.
* **Focus on Inimitable Human Traits:** The future of leadership and education must prioritize qualities machines cannot replicate:
    * Empathy and kindness
    * Critical thinking
    * Ethical citizenship and shared values

> "Technology changes the world, but they would always leave out the other half of that: the world changes technology. Tech doesn't just show up in a vacuum. It arrives in the world as it is with all of our dysfunctions and problems as they exist now." — **Dex Hunter-Torricke**

> "If you are a human whose value is mostly based on just knowing a bunch of stuff which might be objectively true, I suspect you're going to have a really, really bad time in about a decade." — **Dex Hunter-Torricke**

> "The real solution doesn't lie in a set of technological solutions to technological problems, they are in fact societal solutions to societal problems." — **Dex Hunter-Torricke**

briefings.title: The Boardroom’s Biggest Blindspot: Rubrik's CTO Explains Why Cyber Acumen Is Non-Negotiable
briefings.tldr: As non-human identities outnumber human identities 82-to-1, cyber risk has transitioned from a technical hurdle to a core fiduciary responsibility, requiring boards to prioritize "cyber resilience" over simple prevention.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
As non-human identities outnumber human identities 82-to-1, cyber risk has transitioned from a technical hurdle to a core fiduciary responsibility, requiring boards to prioritize "cyber resilience" over simple prevention.

## The Massive Expansion of the Attack Surface
* **Non-Human Identity Explosion:** Rubrik Zero Labs reports a ratio of 82 non-human identities (machines, bots, and AI agents) for every one human worker.
    * **The AI Double Edge:** While "agentic AI" allows for massive scaling and data processing, it creates an unmanaged amplification of risk if guardrails are not in place.
* **Sophisticated Threat Vectors:** AI is enabling threat actors to execute highly authentic social engineering, including "vishing" (voice phishing) and deepfakes that bypass traditional human skepticism.
* **Shadow AI and IT:** Unmanaged "Shadow AI" is already present in most corporate environments, creating hidden vulnerabilities that IT departments cannot currently see or secure.

## The Crisis of Ransomware and Data Recovery
* **Ineffectiveness of Ransom Payments:** Despite the pressure to restore operations, 89% of organizations that pay a ransom do not get their data back. 
    * **The Recovery Gap:** Only 16% of organizations affected by attacks ever fully recover their data.
* **Evolution of Extortion:** Threat actors have moved toward "double and triple extortion," where they not only encrypt data but also exfiltrate sensitive PII (Personally Identifiable Information) or health records to leverage further payments.
* **Attack Frequency:** A survey of 1,600 security and IT leaders revealed that 90% experienced at least one cyber attack this year, with 11% experiencing more than 100.

## Moving from Prevention to "Cyber Resilience"
* **Defining Resilience:** Organizations must shift focus from trying to prevent 100% of attacks to "cyber resilience"—ensuring the business can maintain continuity and recover critical applications quickly after a breach.
* **Quantifying Risk for the Board:** To bridge the communication gap between technologists and the C-suite, risk must be translated into fiscal terms.
    * **Value Economics:** Using frameworks to baseline maturity against industry peers allows leaders to tell the board: "This exposure represents a $500 million incident."
* **Board Composition:** There is an urgent need for "cyber acumen" at the board level. Mariappan suggests that board members must have the expertise to exercise fiduciary responsibility over digital risk.

## Organizational and Industry Vulnerabilities
* **Sector Readiness:** 
    * **High Maturity:** Highly regulated industries like Financial Services and Healthcare are often early adopters of resilience strategies due to compliance mandates.
    * **High Risk:** The Retail sector is currently at high risk due to "technical debt," legacy systems, and complex supply chains involving numerous third-party contractors.
* **The "Department of Know":** Security must transition from the "Department of No" (restricting access) to the "Department of Know" (understanding user behavior and business needs).
    * **Employee Experience:** Security controls should be informed by behavioral telemetry to ensure that "digital native" employees are empowered rather than hindered by authentication protocols.
* **The Skills Gap:** 50% of the current cyber challenge is a "people problem." Organizations require a "top-down, bottom-up" approach to leveling up the cyber knowledge quotient of every employee.

> "Cyber risk is business risk. We want to make sure organizations can maintain business continuity... their critical applications are up and running, their data is secure." — **Kavitha Mariappan**

> "For every one human identity, we're starting to see 82 non-human identities... imagine what that can do for our business, but at the same time, unmanaged, that also presents an amplification of risk." — **Kavitha Mariappan**

> "Security for the longest time has been known as the department of 'No' (N-O). And one of the things we want to do is shift that to the department of 'Know' (K-N-O-W)—get to know, walk in the shoes of the business." — **Kavitha Mariappan**
